The best free time tracking apps

Most time trackers are free for a few users and charge for the parts that turn hours into money: billable rates, invoices and exports. Here is what each free plan includes, from its own pages.

We make Slop Timesheets, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • What the free plan allows: users, projects, tracking
  • Billable rates, invoicing and exports on the free plan
  • Apps for desktop and phone, and working offline
  • Account needed, and where your time entries are kept

1. Clockify

Best for: Small teams who want unlimited tracking free, with desktop and phone apps

Good

  • Unlimited tracking and projects for up to five users
  • Timer, timesheet, auto tracker, Pomodoro timer and idle detection free
  • Track on mobile or desktop even when offline; calendar sync with Outlook or Google

Not so good

  • Billable rates and full exports start on Basic; free export is PDF only
  • Invoicing from tracked time is on Standard
  • Free reports cover a one-month range

Clockify website · Sources: Clockify pricing

2. Slop Timesheets (ours)

Best for: Freelancers who bill by the hour and want rates, totals and invoices free, with no account

A timer or typed durations (1:30, 1.5 or 90m) per customer and project with an hourly rate, week and month totals, CSV, and open hours billed onto a draft invoice in Slop Invoices.

Good

  • Hourly rates, billable and internal time, and invoicing in one click, all free
  • A timer that survives a reload, or type 1:30, 1.5 or 90m
  • Week and month totals and CSV export
  • No account; nothing is uploaded

Not so good

  • No team: one person in one browser
  • No desktop or phone app, no idle detection or calendar sync
  • No sync between devices (move data with a backup file)

Open Slop Timesheets

3. Toggl Track

Best for: Individuals and small teams who want polished timers on every platform

Good

  • Manual and real-time timers, focus mode and calendar integrations free
  • Tasks, boards and task estimates; personal reports
  • Apps on every platform that sync instantly

Not so good

  • Billable rates start on Starter
  • Free plan is for up to three users
  • Team reports and timesheet approvals are paid

Toggl Track website · Sources: Toggl Track pricing

4. Harvest (Free)

Best for: A solo freelancer on Mac or iPhone who wants time, expenses and invoices in one place

Good

  • Time tracking, invoicing and expense tracking on the free plan
  • Apps for macOS, Windows, iOS and Android
  • Stripe, QuickBooks Online and Xero integrations on Teams

Not so good

  • Free plan: one seat and two projects
  • The free plan lists Mac and iOS apps

Harvest (Free) website · Sources: Harvest pricing

Which one to choose

For a small team, Clockify has the most generous free plan: five users, unlimited tracking and apps everywhere. Toggl Track is the most polished for up to three people. Both charge for billable rates.

If you are on your own and bill by the hour, Slop Timesheets gives rates and invoicing free with no account, but only in the browser. Harvest's free plan includes invoicing too, for one seat and two projects.

Questions

What is the best free time tracking app?

For teams, Clockify (up to five users, unlimited tracking) and Toggl Track (up to three users). For a freelancer who wants billable rates and invoices free, Slop Timesheets or Harvest's free plan.

Which free time tracker has billable rates?

Slop Timesheets includes hourly rates free. On Clockify they start on Basic and on Toggl Track on Starter, as their pricing pages say.

Can I turn tracked hours into an invoice for free?

Yes with Slop Timesheets (a draft invoice in Slop Invoices) and Harvest's free plan. Clockify's invoicing is on its Standard plan.

Do I need an account to track time?

Clockify, Toggl Track and Harvest are services you sign up for, which lets them sync your entries. Slop Timesheets needs no account and keeps the entries in your browser.
